overview:
Alabama's 5th District sits deep in Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly fifteen points toward the GOP, and first-term incumbent Dale Strong is seeking another term. He enters the fall with a commanding financial position, holding about $1.4 million on hand after raising nearly $1.5 million, while Democratic challenger Andrew Sneed has roughly $170,000 available. No public polls of the race are available, and no major expert raters have scored it.

Prediction markets give Sneed about a three percent chance of an upset. Sneed has raised a respectable $646,000 for a challenger in a district this red, but his thin cash position limits any late advertising push. Absent an unexpected external shock, Strong's combination of incumbency, district partisanship, and financial dominance makes him a heavy favorite to hold the seat.
